verdict.rationale: Firebase ships extensive CLI (firebase-tools), Admin SDKs, and REST-style APIs covering deploy, Firestore, Auth, Functions, Hosting, Rules, and even an MCP server for AI agents (firebase-docs-7/8/10/20, firebase-gh-1/2/3, firebase-probe-5/6), so most core backend operations doable in the console are also scriptable headlessly. However, probes show no discoverable OpenAPI spec or llms.txt (firebase-probe-1/2), and community reports cite real console-only gaps like poor server-side query support and Security Rules being hard to manage/replicate outside the UI (firebase-comm-4, firebase-comm-5), plus AI-assistance features like Gemini insights and Crashlytics analysis are console-chat bound rather than API-callable (firebase-docs-13/14/15/25). Missing for 10: a documented/discoverable OpenAPI spec, confirmation that all console-only features (analytics insights, Gemini chat assistance) have API equivalents, and independent verification that CLI/API truly mirrors 100% of console capability.
